author: TEDx Talks
description: At 12 years old, I mispronounced one word in class. The whole room laughed. In that moment, I made a silent vow: never again. So I erased myself. I wiped the sacred ash from my forehead before walking through the school gates. I stopped watching Malayalam films on Thursday nights. I even asked my grandfather to turn off the radio station we used to love together. And it worked. Nobody laughed at me anymore. But the house went quiet, and I stopped recognising myself. This is a talk about what happens when survival becomes a permanent address, and what it actually means to grow beyond where you started. Not erasure. Not reinvention. Integration. Sudev is a final year Money, Banking and Finance student who is taking the TEDx stage because he mispronounced a word in seventh grade and, apparently, never fully got over it. The talk is about identity. The therapy is ongoing, but he might finally have an idea of what lies beyond it. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference
title: The Perfect Cage | Sudev Sudheer | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often treat change as a matter of desire and discipline: want it badly enough, stay motivated enough, and you will become the person you aspire to be. But desire fades. Some people can sustain it for hours, others for years, but eventually it depletes. In this talk, I explore a simple metaphor: desire is like a phone battery, and willpower is the charger. Useful, necessary, but ultimately powerless without a source of electricity behind it.
That "electricity" is the deeper force that replenishes us: purpose, faith, responsibility, community, family, or accountability to something greater than ourselves. Drawing from personal experience and ideas inspired by Viktor Frankl, I argue that sustainable transformation does not happen in isolation. It happens when we intentionally shape the influences that shape us.
This talk challenges the myth of radical self-sufficiency and asks a deeper question: what are you connected to that can carry you through your worst day, not just your best on
title: Why Trying Harder Keeps Failing You | Youssef Elderiny | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens when the thing keeping you stuck isn't loss, but the desperate need to understand it? In this talk, I explore the psychology behind our obsession with closure. Why the brain clings to unanswered questions, what that fixation actually costs us, and the quiet but radical decision that changes everything. Drawing on the Zeigarnik effect and my own experiences of being paralyzed by unresolved endings, I reframe closure not as something another person gives you, but as the moment you choose yourself over the question. A talk about uncertainty, self worth, and what it means to step into the unknown. Not after the unfinished stories resolve, but while they are still open. Graduating with a BSc in Psychology, Ive spent the last few years turning academic insight into honest, human conversation. I explore mental health experiences that define our generation, from social comparison to the subtle ways our upbringing shapes who we become. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the
title: The Illusion of Closure | Rayana Suleman | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

author: TEDx Talks
description: The signals that precede major crises are rarely hidden, they're just spoken by people institutions have decided aren't worth hearing. Through three examples spanning the 2008 financial crisis, the Me Too movement, and the Arab Spring, this talk shows that the truth consistently arrives early, through culture, through marginalised communities, through voices that never get counted as data. The next unknown is already broadcasting itself. Sarah Pereira is a third-year Aerospace Engineering student who spends equal time studying the mechanics of flight and the mechanics of how the world misses what is right in front of it. Her TEDx talk asks a simple but uncomfortable question: if the next crisis is already visible in the culture, why do we keep being surprised? From the underground economy to grassroots movements to the music of revolutions, this talk traces the signals that were always there, spoken by the people nobody thought to ask. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED
title: Culture Knows First | Sarah Sidney Pereira | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

description: This talk explores the complexity of being human in a world that often pushes people toward extremes and rigid labels. Drawing from several psychological frameworks, it reflects on how pain, trauma, diagnosis, emotion, and societal expectations can shape identity, self-perception, and the life narratives people come to author. Rather than presenting healing as perfection or the elimination of suffering, the talk explores integration, psychological flexibility, meaning-making, authenticity, and the capacity to hold contradiction with compassion. Audiences are invited to reconsider how they understand themselves, their suffering, and what it truly means to live a more values-aligned, authentic, and fulfilling life. Yahia Ghaleb is an MSc Clinical Psychology student at University of Birmingham Dubai fascinated by the complexity of human experience and the processes that shape distress, healing, and recovery. Influenced by Humanistic and Existential Psychology, Yahia believes in a more co
title: The Courage to Be Complicated | Yahia Ghaleb | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

description: Almost every culture in human history has imagined heaven as somewhere else. Somewhere we're going. A place where the waiting finally ends. And even when we strip the faith away, the structure stays — we all spend our lives reaching for something just ahead of us. A few more years, a few more achievements, a little more peace. And then we'll be there. But what if we've been looking in the wrong direction? What if the heaven we keep chasing was never ahead of us at all? In this talk, I share what I learned the hard way about what that chasing actually does to a life — and what I found when I finally stopped. It's a talk about the cost of always reaching for somewhere else, and the strange, ordinary beauty of being exactly where you are. Aaditya is a student in his final year, with a habit of turning ordinary moments into bigger questions. He is driven by the search for meaning in the everyday. Today he's taking on a question a friend asked   him once and couldn't let go of. This talk w
title: The Heaven I Stopped Chasing | Aaditya Rajesh | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

description: What if the most celebrated institution in human history was actually designed wrong? The data is uncomfortable. Individuals without heavy family obligation take more risks, earn more, and achieve more. Family-related stress accounts for a third of reported anxiety in young adults. The global cost of informal caregiving sits at $10 trillion annually. By every rational metric, the family is a constraint. And yet, I would not be standing on this stage without mine. This talk is about the moment the argument falls apart. About the sacrifices nobody sees. About the phone calls, the deferred dreams, and the people who believed in you before the results were in. The family may not be optimal. But it might be the most important thing we have ever built. A Year 3 Economics student at the University of Birmingham Dubai, he is exactly the kind of person you'd expect to question everything and then surprise you with the answer. Living independently, far from home, he has spent the last three yea
title: Family: Humanity's Biggest Inefficiency? | Alwin Kallely Jose | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens when the finish line disappears before you cross it? This year, the CBSE board examinations were cancelled in the Middle East. Overnight, months of preparation had nowhere to go. What followed wasn't relief or disappointment — it was a question that had been waiting since 10th grade: who are you when you're no longer defined by what you achieve? "Now What?" is an honest and unexpected exploration of identity after the system ends. It's not a talk about bouncing back. It's not about finding yourself. It's not a list of things you should do differently. It's about the parts of you that existed long before any finish line — quietly, in the background, attached to no grade and no goal. The parts that don't announce themselves. The parts you only notice when everything else goes silent. And what you do with them when it does. Rinaaz is a recent high school graduate who once had a sketchbook, a camera, and a growing list of things she'd get to eventually. Most of them are still

description:
When Death Comes is unlike any of Amaan Iqbal Ibrahim's previous TEDx talks.
There are no slides, frameworks, or explicit lessons. Instead, the talk unfolds as a deeply personal spoken reflection that gradually transforms into a live poetry reading.
The experience begins with observations about life, memory, and the quiet rituals people inherit after loss: replaying voices in empty rooms, reaching for phones before remembering, preserving ordinary objects long after they stop being useful, and discovering how absence continues to behave like presence. Through humour, vulnerability, and reflection, the talk explores the strange emotional afterlife of love.
At the center of the story is Theodore Pudding Iqbal Ibrahim — a mischievous kitten whose brief life unexpectedly altered the emotional architecture of Amaan's own. Rather than focusing on loss itself, the talk lingers in what remains afterward: memory, guilt, tenderness, family, prayer, and the unbearable normality that follows grie
title: Beyond Grief | Amaan Iqbal Ibrahim | TEDxUniversity of Birmingham Dubai

description: In Beyond², I reflect on what happened after I achieved the one dream I once believed would define my entire life: becoming a lawyer. Speaking from my experiences travelling alone through Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Seoul, and Tokyo, I explore how achieving the goal did not bring the finality I expected, but instead introduced me to a deeper process of self-discovery and expansion. Through stories of navigating unfamiliar cities, missing the last MTR back from Shenzhen, and being unexpectedly helped by a woman named Kae — who commended me for remaining calm despite being completely lost — I realised that resilience is often built long before we recognise it in ourselves. The talk explores how the trials, detours, and uncertainties I once resented ultimately became the tools that allowed me to grow beyond the limitations I had placed on myself. description: We spend our lives operating under the assumption that softening the truth makes us a good person. We rewrite texts, water down opinions, and hide our real feelings, convinced it protects the people around us. But this constant focus on keeping the room comfortable isn't actually selflessness. Behind our obsession with being "nice" lies a hidden reality: our politeness is rarely about saving others from getting hurt. It is a protective reflex born out of a fear of judgment. We would simply rather fake a smile than deal with the temporary discomfort of someone being mad at us. When we look at how we treat our friends, families, and co-workers, the cost of this compromise becomes undeniable. True connection requires us to stop prioritizing comfort over reality, step out of the roles we play just to be liked, and finally find the courage to speak plainly. As someone who values clarity over comfort, Raisa is taking the stage to deconstruct the 'nice' disguise. Her talk is a wake-up call t

This essential call to action invites us all to redefine "brownness" and unlearn the internal biases we have been taught. Vivemos numa sociedade que estrutura, planeia e otimiza tudo, incluindo o tempo das crianças. Mas e se o ato de brincar sem propósito fosse exatamente o que falta? 

João Miguel, praticante e professor na área do movimento humano, desafia-nos a repensar a forma como vemos a brincadeira física, não como um extra, mas como uma necessidade essencial em qualquer idade. João Miguel desenvolve o seu trabalho em contextos recreativos e desportivos, com especial interesse na preparação física geral e na aprendizagem motora. description:
The Power of One Choice | Gourav Mahipal | TEDxSVIET

Gourav Mahipal didn't come from money. He didn't come from a family that even understood why education mattered. Just a small town in Rajasthan, a lot of uncertainty, and a decision to bet on himself anyway.

That bet got him a good, stable job. And then he quit it — to start something of his own.

Life didn't make it easy. A serious accident left him with injuries so bad that doctors weren't sure he'd ever walk again. Through the recovery, his girlfriend (now his wife) was right there with him, holding things together. But when she had to move away for further education, the distance became too much, and they went through a painful breakup.

So Gourav was left with nothing but himself — a broken body, a broken heart, and a choice to make.

He chose to get back up.

That one choice is now behind government projects that have reached over 30 lakh students across India.

They are packed with nutrients, easy and beneficial to grow, and inexpensive, creating a path to feed 10 billion people nutriously. But... beans have a branding problem. How do you get people excited to eat more beans? One advocacy group built an ambitious campaign to double global consumption of beans (as well as peas, lentils, and other pulses) by 2028. 140+ diverse partner organizations across 70+ countries, working together to amplify and make visible the importance of beans as a solution. The bean stoke is contagious.  Paul Newhnam is a strategic innovator and executive leader with 25+ years of expertise in managing complex stakeholder relationships, designing campaign strategies, and working in the not-for-profit sector. Paul starts movements that make global impact and drive change in sustainability and food systems. Th
title: A win-win-win answer to the age old question: 'What's for dinner?' | Paul Newnham | TEDxBoston

Drawing on his curiosity in social sciences, and his personal experiences with competition, performance and discipline through sports, Vasil will look at a universal social phenomenon and challenge the audience to reshape their understanding of acknowledgement. author: TEDx Talks
description: AI has fundamentally changed education. Students can now produce excellent work without understanding it. This creates a dangerous "illusion of learning," where students produce high-quality work without active cognitive engagement. To thrive in an AI-driven world, schools must urgently redesign how they measure understanding. Moving away from written submissions alone, educators must champion new methods of measuring learning such as verbal assessments, debate, and the real-time defense of ideas. Ultimately, while AI can generate answers effortlessly, it is our responsibility to generate thinkers who can explain, adapt, and reason under uncertainty. Luke Cumbee is an educator, former debate coach, and national speaker focused on the intersection of artificial intelligence and human thinking. After twelve years teaching at Roosevelt High School in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, including a decade of coaching debate, he saw firsthand how real-time argument and explanation deepen learning.
title: The Illusion of Learning: The Cost of Effortless Answers | Luke Cumbee | TEDxSioux Falls

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if there was only one thing standing between you and the best version of yourself? In Fear Forward, Sofia Samper explores how fear—not a lack of talent, intelligence, or opportunity—is often the greatest barrier to reaching our full potential. Through the inspiring story of her father, who at just 19 years old accomplished what many believed was impossible by moving forward despite fear, and her own journey of embracing uncertainty, Sofia challenges the audience to rethink fear as a signal of growth rather than a reason to stop. This talk is an invitation to stop waiting to feel ready and start becoming the person you’re capable of being.
 Sofia Samper is an international student at Bentley University studying Business Economics and Marketing. Originally from Spain and Ecuador, she has traveled to over 20 countries, an experience that has shaped her global perspective and curiosity about people, cultures, and innovation. Passionate about entrepreneurship, consulting, public speak
title: The Best Version of You Is Closer Than You Think | Sofia Samper | TEDxBentleyU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if living to 100 becomes normal?

MIT AgeLab founder Joseph Coughlin explores one of the greatest transformations in human history: the dramatic increase in life expectancy. While science has given us decades of additional life, society has yet to answer a more important question—how do we live those extra years well?

Drawing on decades of research, Coughlin argues that retirement is no longer just about health, wealth, and leisure. Instead, thriving in a 100-year life requires designing meaningful relationships, purpose, community, housing, mobility, and everyday experiences that make life worth living.

Through memorable questions like "Who's going to have lunch with you?" and "Who's going to change your light bulbs?", this inspiring talk challenges us to rethink aging—not as an ending, but as an entirely new stage of life that deserves intentional design. Dr. Joseph Coughlin, or as he is most often referred to, “Dr. Joe,” leads the Massachusetts Institute of Technology AgeLab
title: Living to 100 Isn't Enough: How to Design a Better Life | Joe Couglin | TEDxMIT

description: What if courage isn't something you think your way into, but something you practice with your body? Through martial arts, play, and shared movement, this talk explores how reclaiming our bodies helps us build connection, challenge isolation, and create spaces where we can be brave, vulnerable, and powerful together. Fränz is a Vienna-based sex educator, coach, and martial arts trainer whose work combines reflective exercises and embodied practices with a queer-feminist perspective. They have dedicated their life to creating spaces where people can feel free and authentic, supporting them in navigating challenges that can feel too difficult to face alone. Through fränz.space, Fränz offers workshops and one-on-one sessions that help people reconnect with themselves and others, set boundaries, and recognize their own strength—grounded in the belief that everyone deserves to grow and belong. title: Change begins when we move together | Fränz Fink | TEDxDonauinsel Salon

description:
In her speech, Elizabeth O’Donnell explores the importance of prioritizing personal wellbeing. Through the loss of her daughter, Aaliyah, Elizabeth speaks of her motivation to create Aliyah in Action, an organization designed to distribute self-care items to help families suffering from perinatal, neonatal, and infant loss. Now, with thousands of packaged gifts delivered all across the globe, Elizabeth recounts her experiences and how she was able to stop acting and put herself first. Elizabeth O'Donnell is the founder and executive director of Aaliyah in Action, a nonprofit organization advancing compassionate, equitable support for families after pregnancy and infant loss while working to improve perinatal bereavement care systems nationwide.
